before.heading: Label free downloads, assisted copies and library-only resources separately.
before.intro: A researcher should know whether a yearbook is downloadable or needs staff help before asking for a paid copy. Give each resource its access method and preserve useful file links when organizing the collection.
before.customerQuestion: Can I get this school year online, or should I arrange another way to access it?

decisions.label: Make the free file easy to identify
decisions.body: The public yearbooks are free searchable PDF downloads, with a warning that files are large. Label the school, year, format and actual file-size information where available. Check labels against the volume itself and inventory existing download addresses before renaming or moving files.

decisions.label: Separate the assisted USB service
decisions.body: Explain staff-prepared USB copies with their current per-year and drive charges. Ask for the exact school and years and discuss the appropriate media. A request for several years should not assume they all fit on one drive, and a hidden download link should not push a visitor unnecessarily toward paid assistance.

decisions.label: Show database access requirements
decisions.body: Label Ancestry Library Edition as in-library access and distinguish databases using a library-card sign-in. Put those conditions next to the relevant link so a home researcher understands the route. Where old file addresses change, preserve links or agree a clear replacement instead of leaving broken references.

ownerInputs: Verified school/year file inventory and existing addresses.
Current assisted-copy and drive terms.
Database access restrictions and approved links.
before.sourceBridge: Poplar Bluff Library separates free searchable yearbooks from assisted USB copies and distinguishes in-library databases from card-authenticated resources. Those access methods should be visible before a researcher requests help.
before.limits: Library staff confirm copy arrangements and subscription access. A listed file does not guarantee every requested format. Content and link organization can improve the existing collection; new archive, payment or authentication systems require separate scope.

decisions.label: Compare the actual products

before.heading: Choose a school trip or general group visit before checking the deadlines.
before.intro: Different group types can have different notice periods and reply expectations. Explain those routes separately and keep lunch-space arrangements distinct from the visit itself.
before.customerQuestion: Which planning instructions apply to our group, and is lunch space a separate request?

decisions.label: Compare the group routes
decisions.body: Show school field trips and other group visits with their own current minimums, advance-notice periods and response windows once the owner confirms them. The published example says those windows differ, so one generic group deadline would hide a useful distinction. Avoid inventing the missing figures during rewriting.

decisions.label: Prepare the relevant attendance details
decisions.body: For school visits, explain the approved supervision requirements and ask for aggregate student and accompanying-adult totals. For an adult group, use the appropriate attendance and contact questions. The group’s choice should change the instructions rather than sending everyone a school chaperone checklist.

decisions.label: Arrange lunch space explicitly
decisions.body: Explain the separate lunch-space process beside the school plan. Asking for lunch should not imply that a room is reserved or that the visit has been accepted. Keep the requested date and any meal-space question together for staff review, with the actual confirmation step stated plainly.

ownerInputs: Current school and general-group thresholds and timing.
Approved supervision and attendance questions.
Lunch-space arrangements and confirmation responsibility.
before.sourceBridge: History Museum on the Square in Springfield distinguishes school and general-group timing and separately arranged school lunch space. The precise current windows are necessary inputs before a useful comparison can be published.
before.limits: Staff confirm the visit and lunch arrangements. An inquiry is not a reservation or a promise of a response by an invented deadline. Consolidate generic field-trip guidance where appropriate while retaining the operator-confirmed differences; new scheduling tools need separate scope.

decisions.body: The October 27 source check found at least two weeks’ notice for school trips and three days for general groups of ten or more paying visitors. Keep those advance-request periods separate from reply timing. The school overview says three to five business days for follow-up, while its request form says three; the general-group information says two business days. Have the museum reconcile the school wording before using one response promise across the page and form.

decisions.label: Prepare the relevant attendance details

before.heading: Keep the chosen cabin attached to its facilities and directions.
before.intro: Cabins offered by one company can differ in capacity, kitchen and laundry facilities. Help guests compare the actual units and distinguish shared property access from a private arrangement before following directions.

decisions.label: Build an actual cabin comparison
decisions.body: The public example lists four cabins with differing guest capacities and kitchen or laundry features. Use a verified inventory to name those differences rather than a generic full-property amenity list. A kitchenette should not become a full kitchen through shared wording, and missing capacity figures should be obtained from the owner.

decisions.label: Explain the shared facilities
decisions.body: Describe the pond and pavilion using the current approved rules. The published policies distinguish fishing from swimming and shared pavilion use. A pavilion mention should not look like a private event reservation, and access for one activity should not be treated as permission for another.

decisions.label: Use the cabin location and selected name
decisions.body: The cabin site is distinct from the company’s other rental operations. Keep the selected cabin’s name beside its approved directions and existing booking route. before.answer: Only if the museum confirms that access is part of the event arrangement. A private hall entrance and an evening rental do not establish gallery admission. For your website brief, specify whether the event includes exhibits, which areas open and who confirms that separately.
